title: Koh Larn Beachfront Restaurants 2026 — Eat by the Sea, Thailand
metaDesc: Where to eat right on the sand at Koh Larn near Pattaya, Thailand. Beachfront restaurants at Tawaen, Samae and Tien beaches with deckchairs, rough prices, the vibe of each beach, and tips for beating the crowds — pulled from real reviews.
keywords: Koh Larn beachfront restaurants, Tawaen Beach restaurants, Samae Beach restaurants, Koh Larn deckchairs, Koh Larn seafood
h1:
Beachfront Restaurants on Koh Larn
Eat right by the sea, straight after a swim
intro: One of the nice things about Koh Larn is that you can walk a few steps out of the water and straight into a beachfront restaurant where you eat with your feet in the sand. Many spots rent out deckchairs so you can lie back, catch the breeze, and order food right there. Each beach has its own feel and price range, so we've sorted out which beach suits which kind of meal, with rough prices and a few things worth knowing before you go.

blocks.html: Koh Larn is the island just off Pattaya, about a 30–45 minute boat ride from Bali Hai Pier. The big draw for eating here is that most places sit right on the sand — order grilled prawns, grilled squid and som tam, then sit under the shade by the water with the waves in the background. Several beaches rent deckchairs you can stretch out on, starting around 50–100 THB per day. Before you plan a meal, it helps to know how the beaches differ.

blocks.title: Read this first
blocks.html: Food on the island runs a little pricier than the Pattaya side because everything has to come over by boat. Single dishes mostly land around 150–400 THB, while seafood sold by weight is priced per kilo. Ask the price per kilo and the weight they're weighing out before you order — that way the bill won't catch you off guard.

blocks.text: Tawaen Beach — the most restaurants, the widest choice

blocks.html: Tawaen is the island's most popular beach, with more than 25 restaurants and shops lined up along the walkway behind the sand. There's everything from seafood and made-to-order Thai dishes to som tam and Western food, and many places will take your order while you're lying on a beachfront deckchair. Chairs rent for around 50 THB a day. The trade-off is the crowds at peak times — several thousand people a day — so it feels lively and a bit market-like. If you like the buzz, this is your beach; if you want calm, head to one of the others.

blocks.text: Half a day with a local who knows the lanes — or cooking a dish yourself — teaches you more than just eating. Book ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide.

blocks.text: Koh Larn beachfront spots people talk about

blocks.html: These are the beachfront spots that come up most often in reviews, ordered by popularity and how close to the sea they sit — not a fixed ranking of how good the food is, since taste is personal. Review scores on the island tend not to run high because of the prices and the crowds, but what they share is that you genuinely get to eat right by the water.

items.name: Krua Chaliang Lom (Tawaen Beach)
items.blurb: A much-talked-about beachfront seafood spot on Tawaen with a full sea view. The dish people order most is the spicy blue crab salad. It's quieter at midday but you'll get flies, which comes with the territory at a beach restaurant — come late afternoon to evening for a more comfortable sit.

items.name: Krua Puang Payom (Tawaen Beach)
items.blurb: Another Tawaen beachfront spot with a pretty sea view. The standouts are the deep-fried seafood curry (haw mok) and the sun-dried squid. Reviewers say evenings hit the sweet spot here — good view and a cool breeze.

items.name: Suk Samoe Camping and Bed (Tawaen Beach)
items.blurb: A camping-style spot by the sea on Tawaen, with live music, a cocktail bar, and seafood sets for groups. It's made for settling in with friends for a long evening. Sets start in the low thousands of THB depending on group size — ask exactly what's included before you order.
items.meta: Tawaen Beach · seafood sets/bar · high price

items.name: Anan Seafood (Samae Beach)
items.blurb: A seafood spot on the Samae Beach side, quieter than Tawaen. The go-to orders are garlic-fried prawns and sea bass fried with fish sauce. Good for a relaxed meal without the noise.

items.name: Koh Larn Seafood
items.blurb: A seaside spot focused on whatever fresh catch comes in that day. The crowd favorite is the grilled squid. Right by the water and good for simple seafood that doesn't need much fuss.

items.name: Rabi's Terrace
items.blurb: A chilled seaside spot. People mention the crab fried rice and the squid stir-fried with salted egg. Good for an easy meal with a sea view.

items.name: Sea Space
items.blurb: Has both an air-conditioned zone and an open zone facing the sea, nicely decorated, with desserts to finish the meal. Good if you want to duck out of the sun for a bit but still keep the view.

items.name: Sunset Restaurant
items.blurb: Plays up the sea view and an easygoing vibe, with both à la carte dishes and set menus, and ingredients brought in fresh each day. Good for settling in to wait for sunset.

items.name: Tien Beach spots (cluster)
items.blurb: Tien Beach has around 8–10 Thai and Western restaurants. The vibe is quiet and the water is clear. The deckchairs here are the more comfortable deck-bed style, renting for around 100 THB a day. Good if you want to eat somewhere quiet with a nice view.

items.name: Nual Beach spots (cluster)
items.blurb: Nual Beach, at the far south, has around 5–7 Thai and Western restaurants. It's a small beach with clear water and monkeys around the hillside — keep any food sealed up and don't feed the monkeys. Good for getting away from the crowds.

blocks.title: About deckchair prices
blocks.html: The standard rate for a deckchair/umbrella at Tawaen, Samae and Nual is around 50 THB a day, while Tien has the comfier deck-beds at around 100 THB a day. Some beaches charge 10–20 THB for the toilet and around 50 THB for a shower on top. It helps to bring small cash.

Samae is smaller than Tawaen but breezier and less crowded, with around 25 beachfront restaurants to choose from. Deckchairs rent for around 50 THB. The sand is a touch coarse but fine to walk barefoot. It suits anyone who wants to eat without the noise of Tawaen — good for families or for a long, relaxed sit.

blocks.text: Tien Beach — pretty views, clear water, calm

blocks.html: Plenty of people rate Tien as one of the prettiest beaches on the island with some of the clearest water. It's about a 5-minute walk from the drop-off point, with roughly 8–10 restaurants and a quieter feel than the other beaches. The deckchairs here are the comfortable deck-bed style at around 100 THB a day. It suits anyone happy to walk a little farther for the calm and the better view — though on long weekends it gets busier too, thanks to its reputation for clear water.

blocks.text: Making a beachfront meal worth it — what to eat

items: Grilled prawns / garlic-fried prawns — the island's most popular order; if ordering by the kilo, check the weight and the price per kilo first.
Grilled squid / sun-dried squid — easy to snack on with the sea view, and plenty of places do it well.
Som tam and grilled chicken — the filling, good-value option; many places do grilled chicken with som tam for under 100 THB.
Sea bass fried with fish sauce / steamed with lime — a fish dish worth sharing around the table.
Spicy blue crab salad / mixed seafood salad — sharp, sour and spicy to cut the richness, and a good match for the beach air.

blocks.text: Go early to beat the crowds, book the boat ahead

blocks.html: Weekends and holidays get very busy — the boats from Bali Hai Pier fill up and you'll queue. Most visitors reach the island around 9–10am and head back around 3–4pm. If you want a comfortable meal and a good chance at a decent deckchair, take an early boat around 8–9am — you'll get a beachfront seat before the restaurants fill up, and the water is clearer than later in the morning once the crowds are in.

blocks.title: Straight talk before you go
blocks.html: The water at Koh Larn turns murky on some days depending on the weather and wind, especially after rain or when lots of people are swimming. If you're really after clear water, choose Tien or Nual and come in the morning. · Watersports like jet skis and banana boats are available at every beach — agree on a clear price and check the gear and life jackets before you go each time. · Help keep the beaches clean and carry your rubbish back to the mainland to bin it.

faq.q: Which Koh Larn beach has the best beachfront restaurants?
faq.a: It depends on your style. If you want lots of choice and a lively scene, go to Tawaen with its 25-plus restaurants. If you want to eat somewhere quiet and breezy, go to Samae. And if you're after pretty views, clear water and a calm vibe, choose Tien.

faq.q: How much does a Koh Larn beachfront deckchair cost to rent?
faq.a: Tawaen, Samae and Nual are around 50 THB a day, while Tien has the comfier deck-beds at around 100 THB a day. Some beaches charge 10–20 THB for the toilet and around 50 THB for a shower on top, so bring small cash.

faq.q: Is food on Koh Larn expensive?
faq.a: A little pricier than the Pattaya side because everything comes over by boat. Single dishes mostly run around 150–400 THB, and seafood sold by weight is priced per kilo — ask the price per kilo and the weight before you order.

faq.q: What time should I go to Koh Larn to avoid the crowds?
faq.a: Most visitors arrive around 9–10am and leave around 3–4pm. To skip the boat queue and grab a beachfront deckchair in time, take an early boat around 8–9am — the water is clearer and you can pick a seat before the restaurants fill up.

faq.q: What should I watch out for eating on Koh Larn's beaches?
faq.a: Beach restaurants tend to get flies during the day, so late afternoon to evening is a more comfortable time to sit. The water is murky on some days depending on the weather, and if you do any watersports, check the price and the condition of the gear and life jackets every time. Don't forget to carry your rubbish back to the mainland.
